assessment: The bottleneck broke overnight and nobody was there to see it, and the thing it was blocking arrived in the same window. origin/main fast-forwarded twice at 06:29:33Z and 06:42:26Z after eleven days frozen, four hours after Andrew asked on the board whether to merge - so the answer to the question he asked is that he already acted on it. But refs only prove that main moved, not what moved, and the one fact the whole fleet turns on is whether orders/ is on 1a05afa: the executors on ZoltarOne and ZoltarGenesis read the working tree of main, so that single bit is the difference between three orders becoming reachable and the dispatch branch still being stranded. This lane cannot run git, so rather than infer it I dispatched a read-only probe to the worker, which is the first order this board has issued that exists purely to close a gap in the brain's own eyesight. Meanwhile c-0002.1 came back with the first real number this build has produced against the end goal: the price inside an intraday rank is about 25 minutes older than that rank's own available_at, CI [-27,-24], five times better aligned than the same-bar fill the Streamlit baseline assumes - which is evidence that H9's artefact is real and quantified rather than suspected. Its pre-registered gate still returned STOP_TIMEZONE and the worker refused to re-gate after seeing the result, which is the discipline working; what that leaves on Andrew is a judgement call and no longer a race, because the 6.61M bars behind the measurement are now on disk. Against the charter, Phase 1a's honest-baseline question finally has a measured input, and the only thing still standing between the fleet and unattended execution is that no node runs an executor daemon - both receipts in this fleet's history came from sessions a human started.

items.title: c-0007.1 is no longer a deadline: accept the STOP_TIMEZONE verdict, or approve the corrected gate and a re-measure against the persisted bars.
items.why: The decision as originally put to you was 'name a date before 09-16 or let the 1-minute window close'. Both halves of that premise are gone: the session ran, and 6.61M bars are on disk so the window no longer binds. What is left is the call only you can make. The measured offset is -25 minutes with CI [-27,-24], but the pre-registered gate returned STOP_TIMEZONE because h=0 lost on 2026-08-19, and the worker correctly refused to re-gate after seeing the result. The data do not look like a clock error: 0 of 162 powered runs sits within 10 minutes of -60 and the offset drifts continuously -23..-30 by day. This blocks Phase 6 and it is on the critical path 1a -> 2 -> 3 -> 6.
items.acceptance: c-0007.1 carries a reply from Andrew choosing one of: (a) accept STOP_TIMEZONE, Phase 6 stays stopped and the finding is recorded as resolved-by-stop; or (b) approve the amended gate clause 'does the fine-grid optimum lie within +/-15 min of a clock-error cell other than 0' as a pre-registered amendment with its own FDR entry, and a re-measure against data/cache/prices/yfinance/intraday_1m/ rather than against yfinance. Either answer also states whether the intraday pipeline reads quotes about 25 minutes before it stamps a run, since that decides whether Phase 6 models a fixed or a per-run latency.

items.title: data/cache/prices/yfinance/intraday_1m/ is now the only copy of a measurement that cannot be retaken, and it is gitignored.
items.why: The 6.61M 1-minute bars behind the -25 minute anchor are about 100 MB, gitignored, and unfetchable from yfinance after roughly 2026-09-17. They are what converted c-0007.1 from a race into a judgement call, and they are the input to any re-measure under the amended gate. A routine cache clean or a fresh clone loses them silently, and nothing in the repo records that they matter.
items.acceptance: Either the directory is excluded from every cleanup path and that exclusion is written down where someone who was not here would find it, or the bars are archived somewhere append-only outside the working tree and the archive's location is recorded in docs/ALIGNMENT_ANCHOR.md. A one-line reply saying which is enough to close this.

items.title: The receipt ledger keyed on path, so an ORDER_RESULT that replaced another at the same path was invisible for 12.8 hours.
items.why: The 23:17Z board-mirror recorded one executor receipt when two existed. fleet/bridge/outbox/20260910-2213-zoltarlead-c-0002.1.md overwrote the courier's report at a path the ledger had already marked seen, so a real research result - the first this build has produced against the end goal - sat unmirrored through the whole overnight gap. This is the same failure mode the charter names as evidence replaced by claim, wearing a ledger's clothes: the mirror proved a file had been processed when what it had processed was different bytes. It cost a reporting cycle here; on a refused or halted receipt it would cost a notification.
items.acceptance: data/fleet/board-mirror.json keys executor receipts on path PLUS the order id named inside the file PLUS its written_at stamp, and a fire re-reads the order id of every outbox file it has seen before rather than skipping on path alone. Checkable by replacing any already-mirrored outbox file with a different order's report and confirming the next fire posts a receipt event for the new order id.
